questions.question: Fixed codes ignore order: “books inspire minds” = “qa ve lu”; “stories inspire children” = “ve ro na”; “books delight children” = “qa mi na”. Which extra coded sentence is consistent with all three?

options.label: A
options.text: stories delight minds = ro na lu

options.label: B
options.text: stories delight minds = ro mi lu

options.label: C
options.text: books inspire children = qa ve ro

options.label: D
options.text: children delight books = mi lu qa

questions.explanation: Elimination gives stories=ro, delight=mi and minds=lu. Thus ro mi lu is the consistent extra code.

questions.question: A label stores the complete reversal of BANUR. Which letter occupies the second position from the LEFT in the stored label?
questions.explanation: BANUR reverses to RUNAB. Its second letter from the left is U.

questions.question: Each word has a fixed, distinct code and order is arbitrary. “mela starts early” = “ka ri so”; “mela starts tomorrow” = “ri ka tu”; “early trains arrive” = “so ne pa”. How many different tokens can individually represent “starts” from these statements?
questions.explanation: Mela and starts share the unresolved set ka,ri. Nothing separates those two words, so starts has two possible tokens.

questions.question: Use row then column. Columns 0,1,2; row 0=K,A,R; row 1=N,A,L; row 2=R,K,A. Decode 21-22-02-10-01-12, then exchange the first and last decoded letters. Which final string results?
questions.explanation: The coordinates first give KARNAL. Exchanging only its endpoint letters gives LARNAK.

questions.question: A naming cycle is TRAIN→BUS, BUS→TAXI, TAXI→TRAIN. Each of two clerks applies the naming rule once to the label received. Starting from the real item TAXI, what label does the second clerk return?
questions.explanation: The two required steps are TAXI→TRAIN→BUS. The second clerk returns BUS.

questions.question: In an eight-letter word, positions 1 and 8 exchange, 2 and 7 exchange, while positions 3–6 stay fixed. Which code results from JALANDAR?
questions.explanation: Only the outer two pairs change. R,A remain at the front, LAND stays in the middle, and A,J finish the code: RALANDAJ.

questions.question: Under a fixed +6 shift, the incomplete name H?RI becomes NGXO. Which letter is missing in the original?
questions.explanation: The second coded letter G has rank 7. Undo +6: 7-6=1=A.

questions.question: Successive letters move forward by the first five primes: 2,3,5,7,11. Which code belongs to DIWAS?
questions.explanation: Apply +2,+3,+5,+7,+11, wrapping after Z. DIWAS becomes FLBHD.

questions.question: A five-letter rule maps input positions to output positions as follows: 1→3, 2→5, 3→1, 4→2, 5→4. Which complete output corresponds to MEHAR?
questions.explanation: These arrows specify destinations, not a reading order. Filling output places 1–5 gives H,A,M,R,E, or HAMRE.

questions.question: A mixed code uses P→5, 5→#, #→R, R→8. Replace each ORIGINAL character exactly once. What is the code of P5#R?
questions.explanation: Apply one substitution per original position, without recoding the results. P,5,#,R become 5,#,R,8.

questions.question: The rule +1,-2 alternates within EACH word and restarts after a space. What is the code for SAT PAL?
questions.explanation: SAT uses +1,-2,+1 to become TYU. Restart the same shifts for PAL to get QYM, giving TYU QYM.

questions.question: Codes are fixed, one-to-one and unordered. “safe roads save lives” = “an bo ce du”; “safe buses save time” = “an ef ce gi”; “roads need time” = “bo ha gi”; “lives need care” = “du ha jo”. Which code set represents “buses care roads”?
questions.explanation: The first and third lines give roads=bo; the second and third give time=gi, so buses=ef. The last line gives care=jo, producing ef jo bo.

questions.question: A code is 3 times the number of vowels plus the alphabet-rank sum of consonants. Count repeated occurrences. What is the code for KAPURTHALA?
questions.explanation: There are four vowels, contributing 12. Consonants K,P,R,T,H,L sum to 85, so the code is 97.

questions.question: A number code moves the last digit to the front and leaves the others in order. What is the code of 50736?
questions.explanation: Move only the final 6 before 5073. This gives 65073.

questions.question: A six-letter code adds triangular shifts 1,3,6,10,15,21 to successive letters. Decode the stored output KDYLXM.
questions.explanation: Subtract 1,3,6,10,15,21 position by position. The recovered letters spell JASBIR.

questions.question: An encoder reverses a word and deletes its new first and last letters. For the seven-letter input TEACHER, which five-letter output remains?
questions.explanation: TEACHER reverses to REHCAET. Deleting R and T leaves EHCAE.

questions.question: A word’s code is its first two letters followed by the number of vowel occurrences. A,E,I,O,U are vowels. Select the code for ROPAR.
questions.explanation: The first two letters are RO. O and A are two vowels, giving RO2.

questions.question: A six-letter word is first shifted by +3,-2,+3,-2,+3,-2; then each adjacent pair of coded letters is exchanged. What is the final output for MUKESH?
questions.explanation: The alternating shifts first give PSNCVF. Exchange pairs PS,NC,VF to get SPCNFV.

questions.question: For original digits, add 2 to even digits and subtract 3 from odd digits, wrapping within 0–9 independently. Which string codes 907264?
questions.explanation: 9,0,7,2,6,4 become 6,2,4,4,8,6. No carries are used, so the code is 624486.

questions.question: A numeric message gives cumulative rank sums: 13,14,27,39,40. Each later total includes all earlier letters. What five-letter word does it represent?
questions.explanation: Successive differences are 13,1,13,12,1. These ranks spell MAMLA.

questions.question: Base: K→%,A→3,N→8,E→7,R→9. Test original KANER and apply all actions in order: (1) if both endpoints are consonants, rotate the base code one place right; (2) if there are exactly two original vowels, replace their codes by # at their CURRENT positions; (3) if the original middle letter is a consonant, move the first code to the end. What results?
questions.explanation: Rotate %3879 to 9%387. The moved vowel codes become #, giving 9%#8#; moving its first code to the end yields %#8#9.

questions.question: The key is unknown, but every letter of a word must move by the SAME cyclic shift. Which candidate can be a code of SOLAN?
questions.explanation: Compare position-wise differences. Only AWTIV gives +8 at every position; different shifts in one candidate disqualify it.

questions.question: Three alphabet-opposite pairs below are correct and one is wrong. Identify the wrong pair.
questions.explanation: Opposite ranks must add to 27. G=7 pairs with T=20, so G→S is wrong.

questions.question: For an even-length word, multiply each rank by its mirror partner’s rank and add, counting each mirror pair once. Which number codes AMRITSAR?
questions.explanation: Mirror pairs are A–R,M–A,R–S,I–T. The sum is 1×18+13×1+18×19+9×20=553.

questions.question: Each stored value is the ordinary rank of a letter minus the rank of the preceding letter; the first value is the first letter’s ordinary rank. What sequence stores PATNA?
questions.explanation: Use signed differences: 16,1-16,20-1,14-20,1-14. The groups are 16, -15, 19, -6, -13.
